summary: Revised the ROXY cinema from v1 without changing its massing, tower, sunburst or marquee. The 344 teal side and back panels are now black (the entrance field is muted cyan terracotta), and the posters use only yellow, black and white. I added a light weathering and subtle variation pass to the cream, quartz and blackstone, plus eight planter beds on the pavement in front of the wings. Check shows 0 floating blocks and the renders read as Art Deco with a tower; `build.nbt` is saved and `v1.nbt` is unchanged.
applied: Visible age: `mcd paint` with `weather light` on the cream sandstone, quartz and polished blackstone, and `vary subtle` on the sandstone (rules.txt). The cream and black reads slightly worn and mixed; a stray dripstone block the weathering left behind was swapped back to polished blackstone.

Fewer colour families: the 344 teal side and back panels are now black terracotta between the cream fins; the entrance field behind the sunburst went from saturated cyan concrete to muted cyan terracotta; the posters are now yellow, black and white only (no red or cyan). The palette reads cream, black, gold and one teal accent.

Small details: eight planter beds (azalea, flowering azalea, allium on blackstone-brick bases) on the pavement in front of the wing piers, clear of the street lamps. The existing lanterns, TICKETS and EXIT signs, blade signs and marquee lights were kept.
skipped: Reviewers' name ("Art deco movie theatre with tower"): already matches the brief, so nothing to fix.
Removing the cyan accent entirely: teal and gold are a defining Art Deco pairing and the front needs one cool accent, so it is cut back to the entrance field and slit windows rather than removed.
EXIT signs stay red: they are functional and glowing, and I left them even though mcd palette counts red as an extra accent family.
Moss, cracked or mossy blocks for age: they would not suit a clean 1930s picture palace, so age is only light weathering and block variation.
